values.note: First come, first served. The camping fee is paid before occupying a site, on the arrival date only (online through the DNR's Yodel payment page, yodelportal.com/MNDNR, or in person at any state park ranger station); then choose an unoccupied site and post the campsite card. No self-pay envelopes, and onsite staff cannot take payment.

booking.source: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-forests/fees-reservations.html ('Beginning in 2026, state forest camping fees are paid before you occupy a campsite. Same day advance payment is available on your arrival date, you may not pay ahead for camping on a future date'; 'Upon arrival at the campground, choose an unoccupied campsite'; 'DNR does not accept self-payment envelopes on site or mail-in payments'; group sites alone are reservable, and Kruger is not on the group list), read 2026-11-11

values.note: Minnesota state forest drive-in campsite $17 a night, taxes included, paid the same day before occupying the site. Fees are final (no refunds).

fees.source: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-forests/fees-reservations.html ('Individual and equestrian campsites $17 - $22'; 'Starting in 2026, all forest campgrounds that previously did not charge a camping fee will charge $17 per night ($22 for equestrian)'; 'Fees include taxes'; 'Once paid, camping fees are final, there are no refunds'), read 2026-11-11

sites.source: DNR facility record cmp00041 (camping: 'drive_in_campsites': 18, one of them accessible), read 2026-11-11

hookups.source: DNR facility page cmp00041 ('The campsites are considered primitive, designed to furnish only the basic needs of the camper. Each has a cleared area, fire ring, and table'), read 2026-11-11

facilities.source: DNR facility page cmp00041 ('Vault toilets and drinking water are available'), read 2026-11-11

values.note: Open year-round, but the forest roads are not plowed in winter.

season.source: DNR facility page cmp00041 ('Kruger Campground and Management Unit is open year-round, but the forest roads are not plowed in the winter'), read 2026-11-11

note: Minnesota DNR state forest campground in a wooded hollow of the Zumbro River valley, beside the Zumbro River State Water Trail; hiking, ski and horse trails (no horse camping in the campground). No generators during quiet hours, 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude
